summary.headline: Apollo Pipes Q2 FY27 consol revenue up 31% YoY to INR309.6 crores; consol EBITDA recovered to INR11.5 crores (3.7% margin) from INR3 crores in Q1.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales volume rose 13% YoY to 24,501 tons and revenue rose 31% YoY to INR309.6 crores in Q2 FY27. Consolidated EBITDA recovered to INR11.5 crores from INR3 crores in Q1, though management said margins remain below target. Standalone ex-Kisan EBITDA margin was 5.7%, with Kisan still loss-making at about INR3,700 per ton. The quarter also saw entry into ceramic tiles through the Mazzini Tiles acquisition (76% stake, Morbi), with a plan to build a tiles platform and a 2,88,000-ton plumbing capacity target within two years.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR3 crores in Q1
from loss of about INR9,000/ton in Q1

segments.name: Plumbing (standalone ex-Kisan)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 5.7% in Q2; EBITDA of INR7,000/ton, targeted at INR9,000-10,000/ton in H2 FY27. Management previously cited INR8,000-9,000/ton as last year's average.

segments.name: Kisan (Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Volume steady at 5,000-6,000 tons per quarter; EBITDA loss of INR3,700/ton in Q2. Target breakeven in 6-9 months and INR4,000-5,000/ton positive in FY28 (the company's own estimate at call, with a longer-term aim of INR7,000-8,000/ton).

segments.name: Ceramics (Apollo Ceramics / Mazzini Tiles)
segments.commentary: Newly entered in Q2 via Mazzini Tiles (Morbi, 76% stake, first asset acquired at about 4.5-5x EV/EBITDA). Target return on capital 15-20%; plan for 4-5 assets with INR400-500 crores investment and INR1,000 crores revenue, INR225 crores EBITDA.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: UPVC about 45% of sales, CPVC 15-20% (growing double digits), PPR under 5%; balance from water tanks, window profiles, OPVC and HDPE. North India is about 70% of sales.

guidance_outlook: Standalone EBITDA per ton to reach INR9,000-10,000 in H2 FY27, and INR8,000-10,000 over next 6 months per later remarks; INR8,000-12,000/ton sustained over next 3-4 years.
Kisan: breakeven (0 to +INR1,000/ton) within 6-9 months; INR4,000-5,000/ton positive in FY28; INR7,000-8,000/ton in 2-3 years.
Volume: December quarter flattish QoQ; Q4 FY27 volume targeted at 30,000 tons (10% above Q2/Q3 run rate of about 25,000 tons per quarter), implying about 105,000 tons for FY27.
FY30 revenue guidance INR4,000 crores: INR3,000 crores plumbing and INR1,000 crores ceramics; plumbing EBITDA about INR10,000/ton.

Capacity to rise from 2,40,000 tons to 2,88,000 tons within about 2 years (earlier said 12 months), funded from internal cash flow; new South India plant of at least 50,000 tons with land acquisition in next 6 months, delayed about 2 years.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be better than H1, with monsoon impact over and PVC prices stabilising.
capex_capacity: Varanasi plant newly commissioned and ramping up; already EBITDA-positive, with initial costs front-loaded.
Plan to shut smaller plants at Ahmedabad and Raipur, and later small Bangalore unit once South India plant starts; these are sub-5-acre sites versus 20-30 acre standard plants.
Identified 2-3 land parcels for sale in next 6-12 months, expected to raise about INR130 crores to fund South India capex.

Ceramics: INR300 crores investment plan; INR200 crores equity raise announced; INR100 crores already invested (Apollo Pipes investing about INR70-80 crores in first asset); balance about INR200 crores to come from internal cash flows over 2-3 years.
Window profile business at INR70-80 crores annualised run rate, targeted at INR250-300 crores.
demand_pricing: Q2 saw gradual improvement as PVC polymer price volatility moderated from Q1; government measures (minimum import price on suspension-grade PVC resin, withdrawal of customs duty exemptions) supported domestic market.
Channel inventory was soft; restocking began in last few weeks as prices rose. October run rate similar to Q2, with festival labour shortage and Delhi NCR construction pollution ban as headwinds.
Industry volumes flat for top 4 listed players in H1; Apollo grew in line with industry (about 5%) in recent years; market share about 4% after earlier reaching 2.5%.
Management cites aggressive pricing and idle HDPE capacity from government infrastructure segment flowing into trade markets as causes of industry EBITDA compression.
Realisation assumed around INR1,25,000 per ton for plumbing business in 2030 planning.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter tiles, which geographies, and how to scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees tiles as a building-materials extension. Strategy is acquiring profitable operating Morbi assets already supplying 7-8 top brands, with contract manufacturing for organised brands and no near-term own brand; Morbi has INR25,000-30,000 crores of tile output, of which about INR10,000 crores is sold to top 10 branded players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for H2 and next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone EBITDA of about INR7,000/ton in Q2 to be lifted to INR9,000-10,000/ton in H2 FY27, helped by Varanasi ramp-up and closure of Ahmedabad and Raipur units. Kisan to breakeven within 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions available at lower prices due to Morbi stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Target valuation is 4-7x EV/EBITDA; first asset was acquired at about 4.5-5x. Target assets must be profitable with long-term contracts with organised players.

qa_highlights.question: How to fix Kisan?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes have risen to 5,000-6,000 tons per quarter from 3,000-4,000 at acquisition, but profitability has not. Management is cutting factory and corporate costs and says it needs better industry dynamics; a business plan is ready.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook and CPVC performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY27 volume targeted at 30,000 tons, implying about 105,000 tons for FY27. CPVC grew double digits in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Funding and stake strategy for ceramics?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority stakes (about 75-80%) with Apollo managing operations; Mazzini at 76% with the rest callable in 24 months. Product mix target 80% domestic, 20% export. Funding from INR200 crores equity raise plus internal cash flows; no further fund raise needed for the INR500 crores acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the competitive advantage versus Supreme, Astral and Finolex?
qa_highlights.answer: Highest market share in North India (about 70% of sales); pricing held at par with top players. West lagged due to Kisan; South India capex delayed about 2 years. Brand strength in Central and East India is to be leveraged via Varanasi.

risks_watch: Kisan remains loss-making at INR3,700/ton EBITDA loss; breakeven target depends on industry pricing and PVC volatility.
Standalone margin target of INR9,000-10,000/ton versus INR7,000 in Q2 and INR8,000-9,000 last year.
South India greenfield delayed about 2 years; land not yet acquired.
Ceramics execution risk: first major move into a new category, with the first asset at about 76% stake and 4-5 more acquisitions planned.
Dependence on PVC price stability; channel restocking depends on prices holding.
Q4 FY27 volume target of 30,000 tons is a 20% step-up from the 25,000-ton run rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term plan and recovery trajectory, but openly cautious on current margins (described as below desired levels) and on Kisan, which management admits has underperformed. Some answers were hedged on external factors such as PVC prices and industry conditions.
key_quotes: Needless to say, the margins are still below the levels we want.
And we remain committed to funding this expansion from internal cash flow without leveraging the balance sheet.
We will not leave it to the existing promoters to manage these assets, point number 1.
So we have ensured that our North India pricing doesn't get disturbed because of competition, and we are able to maintain industry volume growth also in that market.

adds.what: Capacity rise from 2,40,000 t to 2,88,000 t/yr (plumbing), funded from internal cash flow
New South India plant of at least 50,000 t/yr (land acquisition in next 6 months; delayed about 2 years)
Ceramics platform: 4-5 tile assets with INR400-500 crore investment, INR1,000 crore revenue target (Mazzini Tiles, Morbi, 76% stake, first asset acquired)
Varanasi plant newly commissioned and ramping up (already EBITDA-positive)

growth.why: Guided FY27 volume of about 105,000 t (Q4 at 30,000 t, ~10% above the ~25,000 t quarterly run rate) and H2 standalone EBITDA of INR9,000-10,000/t, backed by a 48,000 t capacity rise to 2,88,000 t within about 2 years and the new ceramics platform, but the South India plant is delayed about 2 years and funding is only partly specified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA per ton guided up from INR7,000 in Q2 to INR9,000-10,000 in H2 FY27 on Varanasi ramp-up and Ahmedabad/Raipur closures; Kisan loss to narrow from INR3,700/ton to breakeven within 6-9 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity to rise from 2,40,000 to 2,88,000 tons (+20%) within about 2 years, funded from internal cash flow; Varanasi already commissioned and ramping; South India plant of 50,000+ tons delayed about 2 years with land purchase due in 6 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 FY27 volume targeted at 30,000 tons vs ~25,000 tons run rate (about 10-20% step-up), implying ~105,000 tons for FY27; December quarter flat QoQ and H1 volume up 4% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land acquisition for South India plant due within 6 months and 2-3 land parcels (about INR130 crores) to be sold within 6-12 months to fund capex; ceramics INR300 crore plan with INR200 crore equity raise already announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on current margins (below target) and Kisan (loss of INR3,700/ton), with October run rate similar to Q2 and festival and construction headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY27 volume target of 30,000 tons is about 20% above the 25,000-ton run rate, and H2 standalone EBITDA of INR9,000-10,000/ton compares with INR7,000 in Q2, with PVC prices and channel restocking dependent.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Window profile business targeted at INR250-300 crores from INR70-80 crores run rate, and ceramics platform entry via Mazzini Tiles, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Ceramics platform via Mazzini Tiles (Morbi)
rows.why: First asset acquired at about 4.5-5x EV/EBITDA, with 4-5 assets planned for INR400-500 crores investment, INR1,000 crores revenue and INR225 crores EBITDA; INR200 crore equity raise announced.

rows.label: Kisan breakeven
rows.why: Kisan loss narrowed to INR3,700/ton in Q2 from about INR9,000/ton in Q1 and target is breakeven to +INR1,000/ton in 6-9 months, but depends on industry pricing and PVC volatility.

rows.label: Closure of Ahmedabad and Raipur plants
rows.why: Sub-5-acre sites to be shut versus 20-30 acre standard plants, and later Bangalore unit, supporting the INR9,000-10,000/ton H2 margin target.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term plan (FY30 INR4,000 crore revenue, ceramics platform) and the H2 margin recovery, but cautious on current margins below target, Kisan underperformance and PVC price dependence; analysts pressed on the ceramics strategy and funding.
